THE SHOPKEEPER'S CATALOGUE

Complete Economy & Equipment Reference

This catalogue lists the prices, slot values and key statistics of the goods, weapons and armour available across Arneyan.

Currency & Inventory Notes

  • Conversion Rate: 1 Platinum (pp) = 10 Gold (gp) | 1 Gold (gp) = 10 Silver (sp) | 1 Silver (sp) = 10 Copper (cp)
  • Selling: shopkeepers generally buy at about half the listed price, though no two merchants are alike. Gems and art sell at full value (a fence pays half).
  • Prices throughout reflect wartime inflation and may run higher than standard fantasy pricing conventions.
  • All carrying capacity is tracked with the slot-based inventory system (18 slots, or 20 with Strength 16+; see The Arneyan Codex), not weight. Standard gear = 1 slot. Heavy/bulky/two-handed items = 2-3 slots. Ammunition = 30 pieces per slot. Coins = 100 per slot. Minor/light items bundle up to 5 of the same type per slot. Worn armour and carried weapons count against it.
  • Items without a listed slot value (mounts, vehicles, lodging, services, large storage furniture) are not personally carried and don't apply to the grid.

Rarity

  • Every item in this catalogue is Common unless its name carries a tag: [Uncommon], [Rare], [Very Rare] or [Unique]. Rarity governs availability, not power, and the listed price does not change.
  • [Uncommon]: stocked only in cities, guild halls and specialist shops. Elsewhere a shopkeeper can order it in (1d4 days) if one is within reach.
  • [Rare]: never on a shelf. It must be commissioned from a master (1d4 weeks), tracked down through a contact, or found. The GM decides whether it can be had at all.
  • [Very Rare]: a handful exist in a region. Found through adventure rather than commerce; the listed price is a guide, not a sale.
  • [Unique]: one of a kind, an artefact or a named item. Never for sale.
  • Rule of thumb for magical goods, alchemy and spell components: Common up to 150 gp, Uncommon up to 500 gp, Rare up to 5,000 gp, Very Rare above. Exceptions: mundane gear is Common unless tagged for availability (exotic arms, plate, firearms), restricted goods such as poisons are never below Uncommon, and components priced per HD are Uncommon at least. The GM may raise or lower any item's rarity for a region.

How Magic Items Work

  • Use: An item works as its description says for anyone holding, wearing or wielding it. There is nothing to attune.
  • Carrying: 1 slot unless the entry says otherwise (rings, wands and other small items bundle 5 to a slot).
  • Magic weapons and armour: They count as magic against nonmagical Resistance. A weapon's +N is a number added to attack and damage rolls (an exception to the Advantage rule). Armour's +N adds to AC. No weapon, armour or shield is ever better than +3.
  • Identify: The Identify spell reveals one property per casting. Otherwise powers reveal themselves through use or research. Anyone can use an unidentified item, but that is a risk: the GM describes what happens, and curses stay hidden until they show.
  • Charges: Wands have charges and no recharge. Staffs regain 1d4 charges at dawn. When a wand or staff reaches 0 charges, roll a d20: on a 1, it crumbles to dust.
  • Value: Iconic items have a replacement value but are never stocked by shops. Uniques are never for sale.
  • Curses: The GM keeps them secret. No item in this book is labelled cursed. Remove Curse can free the user, but the item remains cursed.
  • Destruction: An item is destroyed only as its entry says, or by GM ruling.
